HomeEssentials Retail Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Retail Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Retail Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer; and David Patel, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Johnson.

Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Retail Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: We achieved comparable store sales growth of 3.2%, supported by improvements in store traffic and conversion rates, while advancing our store fleet optimization, omnichannel integration, and supply chain efforts that together contributed significantly to our margins and sales momentum.
2. E-Commerce Growth: Our digital channels saw robust expansion, with omnichannel fulfillment like BOPIS and curbside pickup driving higher order values and store traffic, pushing digital penetration to 28% of total revenue.
3. Store Performance: Brick-and-mortar remains our core, with over 70% of sales, enhanced by labor efficiencies and remodels that improved productivity and customer experience across our 1,200 stores.
4. Marketing Initiatives: Our loyalty program reached 45 million active members, boosting redemption rates and lifetime value, complemented by targeted regional marketing and value-focused assortments.
5. Supply Chain Optimization: Initiatives like new DCs, RFID rollout, and vendor diversification reduced costs, shrink, and lead times, positioning us lean entering the holidays.
6. Loyalty Program Update: Membership growth and personalized engagement lifted repeat purchases and margins, integrated with sustainability efforts like our Green Thread line.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more details on our financial results.

John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.82 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 39.0%, primarily driven by lower markdowns, private label mix shifts, and supply chain savings. Operating expenses were $795 million, representing 28.2% of revenue. Net income was $220 million, or $1.00 per share. We generated $380 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently at 12 weeks of supply, leaner than the industry average of 14 weeks.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Before opening the floor to questions, let me expand on our outlook and key drivers, as these tie directly into the aspects Mike highlighted. As always, forward-looking statements are subject to safe harbor provisions and risks in our SEC filings, such as macro headwinds, supply chain issues, and shifting consumer sentiment.

We're cautiously optimistic, anchored by omnichannel execution, disciplined inventory, and our resilient brick-and-mortar base driving over 70% of sales. For Q4 ending January 2025—our key holiday quarter—we expect consolidated comparable sales growth of 2.5% to 4.5%, with stores at 1.5% to 3.5% and digital accelerating to 8% to 12%. This follows Q3's +3.2% total comps, with 25 basis points better traffic and 75 basis points higher conversion from in-store digital kiosks.

Top line for Q4: $2.85 billion to $2.95 billion, or 3% to 6% growth, including 150 basis points from 25 net new small-format stores averaging 15,000 square feet, which outperform legacy formats by 15-20% on four-wall profits. Full FY2025 revenue: $11.8 billion to $12.2 billion, or 4% to 6% growth, assuming unemployment below 4.5% and PCE inflation in low-2s.

Gross margins for Q4: 39.0% to 39.8%, up 50-130 basis points, from markdowns at 18% of sales versus 22% last year, higher-margin private labels up 12% to 28% of assortments, RFID across 85% of 1,200 stores cutting shrink 22% and boosting replenishment to 96%, enabling 8% leaner inventories. FY25 margins: 39.5% to 40.2%, aided by our new 800,000-square-foot Ohio DC at 25% utilization, saving 50 basis points on freight via Union Pacific rail.

Adjusted operating income Q4: $285 million to $315 million, or 10.0% to 10.7% margins, up from 9.4%, with SG&A at 28.5% to 29.0% despite some deleverage, thanks to AI scheduling optimizing labor 10% like at Target. FY25 op margins: 10.2% to 10.8%, with $75 million savings from Store 2.0 remodels—200 of 400 done, featuring AR try-on mirrors boosting conversion 18% and Nike/Levi's shop-in-shops lifting category comps 5-7%.

EPS Q4: $0.85 to $0.95 at 25.5% tax and 220 million shares after $200 million buybacks. FY25 EPS: $3.60 to $3.90, up 12-20% from $3.20, backed by $850-950 million free cash flow at 7.5-8.5% yield. Capex $450 million on 60 stores, DC automation, EV chargers at 30% of sites.

Regionally: Sunbelt (35% sales)—5-7% comps on migration, tourism, DFW back-to-school; Midwest/Southeast 3-5% on gas prices aiding tools/decor; Northeast/West Coast flat to +2% on office traffic down 10-15% per Placer.ai, countered by pop-up hubs with influencers spiking traffic 30%.

Strategically for FY25: omnichannel acceleration with BOPIS at 22% digital sales targeting 30%, RFID visibility like Macy's/Kohl's; supply chain with 40% imports to Vietnam/Mexico, China under 50%, $40 million vendor rebate savings; sustainability/loyalty with Green Thread at 15% apparel using recycled materials, 8% eco-share per NPD, 45 million loyalty actives at 65% redemption, 4x LTV.

Macro risks: Conference Board confidence at 108, vulnerable to Fed pauses; 2-3% discretionary pressure per McKinsey, Temu/Shein on low-end; upside from stimulus/weather. We're returning 50% FCF via buybacks/dividend at 2.2%, eyeing M&A like Bed Bath remnants.

Turning to omnichannel progress, a cornerstone for seamless experiences. Digital sales hit 28% of revenue, up from 22%, lifting traffic and margins. BOPIS grew 32% to $1.2 billion, 62% of e-comm, AOV $145 (18% over pure online $123) via AI upsells like appliance bundles +12% baskets; 97% success via OMS/WMS. Curbside up 45% to 2.8 million orders, 28% digital, AOV $162 highest, +250 bps margins no shipping; 2x loyalty points for 15% repeat lift.

Regional: Southeast 68% BOPIS (320 stores, DoorDash hybrids); Midwest 55% improved via micro-DCs cutting times to 45 min +4.2% SSS; West Coast 95% SLAs, 35% curbside clawing 2 share points per Nielsen. EdgeStore on Google Vertex AI cuts no-shows 22%, RFID 60% SKUs 99% accuracy; omni +180 bps comps, 40% add-ons in-store. FY25 target: 35% digital, 70% BOPIS/curbside, $150 million for micro-DCs/AR try-on like IKEA.

On comp sales guidance: Q3 was +4.2% with 1.8% traffic, +150 bps conversion to 28.5%, +2.1% AUR despite -0.5% softlines from weather. Q4: +3.0% to +5.0% on omni traffic (BOPIS 22%, 35% add-ons via POS), owned brands +12% to 42%, 150 new SKUs holiday-timed. Sunbelt +5-7% housing 4.2M units/NAR; Midwest +3-5% remodels; West flat-+2% insurance/wildfires. FY25 raised to +3.5-+4.5%. Tailwinds: freight -40% Drewry, turns 5.2x, sell-through >85%. Capex $250M: 75 stores, 100 remodels, SymphonyAI planograms +200 bps comps. Risks: tariffs, wages, Fed; monitoring HomeEssentials Index at 72.

Key strategic initiatives: Three pillars added 250 bps to Q3 comps +110 bps margins. Store 2.0: closed 25 underperformers ($45M savings), renovated 150 flagships with maker spaces +12% ticket, RFID self-scan -35% throughput; renovated +7.8% comps, turns 6.1x; 200 more by YE, 18-20% ROI. Sunbelt 6.5% comps HVAC; Northeast stemmed declines +8% traffic.

Omni: Seamless Home BOPIS +42% to 28% e-comm $2.1B Q3, +15% traffic; same-day curbside 85% <$100; app 4.2M downloads +55%, 22% conversion; 18M loyalty 60% sales +320 bps margins; digital 22% revenue -22% logistics to $4.50/order.

Supply chain: New Dallas/Atlanta RDCs 1.2M sq ft, Honeywell automation -28% lead times to 4.2 days, availability 96.5%; P&G/LG contracts 8-10% cuts 40% assortments; inventory -12% $1.8B 10.8 weeks; $65M EBITDA YTD +40 bps. Synergies: AR zones to AI forecasting -25% stockouts; 60% stores solar/LED -18% energy; 50 EV chargers ChargePoint.

Expect 400-500 bps H2 comp acceleration, +75-100 bps margins; capex 4.5% sales.

Earnings guidance context: Q3 sales $2.55-2.65B beat at 3-6% organic vs. peers flat-+2%; comps +2.5-+4.5%; margins 38.5-39.2% +50-100 bps freight -15%, Memphis DC, ForgeHome 28% +500 bps, turns 5.2x. SG&A 26.8-27.3%, StoreFlow -12% OT; op income $420-460M, EBITDA 15.2-15.7%; EPS $1.22-1.32.

FY24 raised: sales $10.7-10.9B +2-4% +150 bps new sq ft; comps +2.0-+3.5%; margins 38.7-39.3% private 30% Vietnam/Mexico; SG&A 27.0-27.5% $120M omni curbside 22%; op income $1.75-1.85B EBITDA $1.95-2.05B 18.2%; EPS $4.65-4.85 +8%.

Pillars: Endless Aisle kiosks/app 30% digital Walmart-style; RFID 80% -22% shrink; ForgeRewards 18M +25% 45% repeat.

Risks: unemployment >4.2%, commodities +5-8%, Amazon/Wayfair; upside eco GreenForge/M&A.

Labor costs/store payroll: Q3 payroll 11.2% sales -70 bps YoY, 6th quarter leverage +25 bps margins; costs +2.1% $18M vs. 3.8% wages; sales/labor hour $142 +4.6% > peers $135. Peaked 12.8% Q1'23, now wages +4.2% turnover 62%; benefits flat wellness.

Productivity: hours/sq ft -3.2% 0.18, comp/store +1.5%; omni 18% sales monetizes capacity. EssentialsOptix AI UKG to 85% stores -15% OT to 6.8%, -22% under-schedules; RPA pilots -10-15 hrs/week +40 bps.

Regional: Northeast 12.5% cross-train +5.8%/hr; Midwest/Southeast 10.4/10.1% low wages; CA 13.1% pods +90 bps. NPS 78; manager bonuses 20% payroll ratios; upskilling 65%. Q4 +50-75 bps; risks min wage, variable comp 12%.

This positions us for 7-8% margins FY26 >5.5% sector.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa Chen, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to David Patel to discuss store operations.

Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, John. This quarter, we launched our ForgeHome line, which has seen strong uptake with 12% growth and now represents 28% of assortments, delivering 300-500 basis points of gross margin expansion through favorable mix shifts and resonating in owned brands like EssentialsPro paint and modular storage. Early holiday SKUs in organization are timed for gifting, and eco-lines like Green Thread using 100% recycled polyester captured 8% eco-share per NPD. We're excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in high-margin categories like appliances and wellness home.

David Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented Store 2.0 remodels in 200 locations with interactive AR try-on mirrors boosting conversions 18%, shop-in-shops with Nike and Levi's lifting comps 5-7%, maker spaces for DIY +12% tickets, RFID self-scan -35% throughput, and AI scheduling for 10% labor optimization without hurting NPS at 78. Small-format urban prototypes and EV chargers are driving 15-20% higher profitability and traffic spikes. We're seeing positive results across renovated units at +7.8% comps.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of omnichannel initiatives like BOPIS and curbside on your sales?

Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Jane. Absolutely, omnichannel has been transformative, contributing 180 basis points to comps with BOPIS at 62% of digital and curbside delivering highest AOVs and margin lifts. It's not just digital growth—40% of pickups lead to in-store add-ons, and with EdgeStore AI and RFID, we're hitting 97-99% accuracy, positioning us ahead of peers for FY25 35% digital penetration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Bob Smith (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, Bob. For Q4, we're guiding 3.0% to 5.0% comps, accelerating from Q3's 4.2%, with omni traffic, owned brands, and regional strength in Sunbelt at 5-7%. FY25 raised to 3.5-4.5%, supported by capex efficiencies and inventory turns, outpacing NRF holiday averages.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alice Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alice Johnson (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Sure, Alice. Our new Ohio and regional DCs, rail partnerships, and vendor scorecards have cut freight 50 bps, lead times 28%, and shrink 22% via RFID at 85%. Diversifying to Vietnam/Mexico saves $40 million FY25, with availability at 96.5%—key for holidays with lean 12-week inventory.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great to hear, Tom. Loyalty hit 45 million actives with 65% redemption driving 4x LTV and 320 bps margin lift; ForgeRewards 2.0 personalization boosts repeats 45%, 60% of sales, integrated with 2x points for curbside and eco-products like Green Thread gaining share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Wong with Citi. Please go ahead.

Chris Wong (Citi):
How are labor efficiencies playing into your margin outlook?

John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Chris. Store payroll leveraged 70 bps to 11.2% via EssentialsOptix AI reducing OT 15%, sales per hour $142, and omni monetization. Expect another 50-75 bps Q4, supporting 10.2-10.8% FY25 op margins despite wages.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
